overall.summary: Every stated number, count and threshold reproduces and no hypothesis is contradicted; the weakenings are shape words and readings: the sodium minimum is at 139 not 138, the age curve has a step at 75-85 for men rather than a steady rise, the BMI curve has a cliff at 20-23, the direct sodium tilt is not gentle, the noise effect is small only on average, and the renal unit's 'either input open' reading holds for under half of those rows.

low_sodium.why: An exact hyponatraemia hinge: on for exactly the 223 rows with sodium at or below 134 mmol/L and growing linearly as sodium falls (concept R2 1.00).

high_sodium.why: Unit 1173 is an exact hypernatraemia hinge at 140 mmol/L (635 rows, 0 exceptions); the second unit is a shallower sodium hinge mixed with the noise column, which the hypothesis states.

age_bmi.why: Probes confirm 'older and leaner opens it': at BMI 22 the near copy grows with age and the high copy opens at 70, at BMI 34 both stay shut through age 70 and 90.

sex_diabetes_gate.why: Open only for non-diabetic men (0 exceptions in 1500 rows) and widening with age and leanness, closed by high sodium, as probed; the concept captures when it opens (AUC 0.94) better than how wide (R2 0.36), which the hypothesis covers in words.

renal_228.why: Low sodium or an open gate is needed for it to fire (0 exceptions), but not enough: it fires for 215 of the 457 rows where either is open, as a threshold on their sum plus creatinine and smoking.

bp_hr.why: The discordance reading holds on constructed cases and on training rows: raising pressure raises the score for 99.6% of rows at a pulse of 55 and lowers it for 100% at 100, and the four pressure-by-pulse cells order as stated.

direct.why: A linear sum of nine direct input edges; it is described by its coefficients, which reproduce, and has no single reading (the record says so).
